title: BOE Sees Threat to Government Bonds in AI Growth Miss
key_facts: The BoE's Financial Policy Committee said the likelihood interconnected vulnerabilities crystallise has risen.
It pointed to re-escalation of the Iran conflict and higher oil, gas and refined product prices as a protracted negative supply shock.
Bond yields reached levels not seen since 2008.
The committee noted a 'rapid increase' in AI-related debt issuance; Morgan Stanley estimated about $450 billion globally, double 2025.
AI and chip stocks fell sharply in July but markets stayed orderly; a bigger shock could cause a sharper repricing.
Governor Andrew Bailey, in an article on AI risks, urged 'rigorous model testing' before and after deployment ahead of tighter regulation.
The Countercyclical Capital Buffer stays at 2%.
quote_evidence: The likelihood that interconnected vulnerabilities in the financial system crystallise has risen.
Understanding, testing and establishing credible points of intervention must come first.
why_it_matters_hint: A central bank is treating AI-related borrowing as a financial stability risk.
notes: Possible mismatch with the WSJ headline.
